lesson.subject: inquiry
lesson.title: Pitch It
lesson.subtitle: Shark Tank | Term 4 Week 8, Session 7
lesson.footer: Shark Tank | Grade 5 Inquiry | Week 8 Session 7

plan.curriculum: Victorian Curriculum Economics and Business, Levels 5 and 6: presenting a business idea to people who might invest; English, Level 5: planning and delivering a short spoken presentation for an audience
plan.shape: 15 minutes explicit, 40 minutes team time: Carson's pitch again with a new lens, the six-part pitch recipe on Pocket Pal, a quick round, then teams write and rehearse their pitch
plan.criticalFeature: a pitch runs in order, hook, problem, product, upcycled, price, ask, and the ask is for investment, never a sale
decisionPoints: the Which part of the pitch? round
the choice check: the strongest ask
the exit board: a hook and an ask for a new product
plan.anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 6? Say: the 4 Ps are Product, Price, Place and Promotion, and your team has a tagline. Your team tells you both before you write your part.

studentTools: Each team's prototype, poster and Marketing Plan
manipulatives: A timer that teams can see, for 60 to 90 second rehearsals
The Pocket Pal model for the I Do demo
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: The pitch recipe in order: Hook, Problem, Product, Upcycled, Price, Ask
Rehearsal spaces around the room, one per team
videos: Locker Board on Shark Tank US, watched again from Session 1 (youtube.com/watch?v=IDpfl2aGruE)

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your team's pitch planner: name the parts, write your lines, time it and fix it.
resources.title: Pitch Planner
resources.subtitle: Hook. Problem. Product. Upcycled. Price. Ask.

example.prompt: Who's ever found their hat on the floor? Which part of the pitch?
steps: It's the first line, and it's a question.
It grabs the audience before the facts.
A line that grabs attention is the hook.

items.prompt: A team pitches Sock Snake, a draught stopper. Name each part.
rows: Cold air sneaks under classroom doors all winter.
Brrr! Ever had cold feet at your desk?
Invest your tokens in Sock Snake and keep every classroom cosy.
Every Sock Snake is stuffed with old socks.
answers: Cold air sneaks under classroom doors all winter.
Brrr! Ever had cold feet at your desk?
Invest your tokens in Sock Snake and keep every classroom cosy.
Every Sock Snake is stuffed with old socks.

example.prompt: Write the price line for Pocket Pal.
steps: Say what it costs to make: $2.
example.answer: It costs $2 to make and sells for $8.

items.prompt: Write your team's pitch. Give every member a part.
answers: a question or surprise that grabs attention
the problem and who has it
cost to make and selling price

example.prompt: Pocket Pal's pitch took 2 minutes. What should the team do?
steps: Cut extra words from the longest part, then time it again.
example.answer: Cut the longest part, then time it again.

items.prompt: Time your pitch. How many seconds did it take? Is it between 60 and 90?
items.answer: A time in seconds, with a yes or a plan to cut or add.

items.prompt: Ava wrote the ask for Sock Snake. Find the mistake and fix it.
work: Please buy a Sock Snake. They're only $5!
items.answer: The sharks invest, they don't buy. Fix: Invest your tokens in Sock Snake and keep every classroom cosy.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: get ready for the sharks' questions.
resources.title: Extension: Answer the Sharks
resources.subtitle: After the pitch, the sharks ask questions. Be ready.

sections.title: Plan your answers
sections.intro: A strong answer is short, honest and uses evidence: your test results, your Token Test, or your costs.

example.prompt: A shark asks Pocket Pal: why not just use a normal bag hook?
steps: Name the evidence: our Token Test.
Say what it showed: 15 out of 20 Grade 6s lose things off hooks.
Link it back: Pocket Pal holds them in a pocket, not on a hook.
example.answer: Our Token Test showed most kids lose things off hooks. Pocket Pal holds them in a pocket instead.

items.prompt: Write your team's answer to each shark question.
rows: How do you know people want it?
Why is upcycling better for this product?
answers: How do you know people want it?
evidence from the Token Test or survey
a failed test and the fix that worked
Why is upcycling better for this product?
it saves natural resources and money

example.prompt: A shark says: I don't think anyone needs this. What's a calm reply?
steps: Thank them, then give one piece of evidence.
Thanks. Actually, 12 people in our survey said they'd use it.
example.answer: Thank them, then give one piece of evidence.

items.prompt: A shark says your price is too high. Which reply is best?
options: Thanks. It costs $3 to make, so $6 still makes a profit.
items.explain: The second. It stays calm and uses evidence: the cost to make shows the price is fair.

steps: Hook: Have you ever found your hat on the floor?

example.answer: Have you ever found your hat on the floor? Hats and bottles fall off bag hooks every day.

items.prompt: Finish each sentence for your team's product.
rows: It costs ___ to make and sells for ___.
answers: It costs ___ to make and sells for ___.

slides.notes: Pitch week. One line: today every team writes and rehearses the pitch it gives the sharks on Shark Tank Day.

Prototypes, posters and Marketing Plans out before the bell. Six cue cards per team. A visible timer. Cue the Locker Board clip. Print the Worksheet one per team, plus a few Extension and Supported copies.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning how to pitch a product so people want to invest.
successCriteria: I can name the six parts of a pitch.
I can write my part of our team's pitch.
I can deliver our pitch with a clear voice and a demo.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: In two weeks you face the sharks.
Today you write what you'll say.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Fifteen minutes with me, then forty minutes to write and rehearse.
notes.prep: 15 minutes explicit, 40 team time. SC1 the six parts for all; SC2 writing a part is the core; SC3 delivery. Anchor: Find a problem. Upcycle a fix. Pitch it.

slides.title: How does Carson start?
slides.prompt: Turn and tell: how did Carson grab the sharks at the start?

notes.answer: open - his opening words, or showing the board straight away
beats: PLAY from 0:00. Pause at about 0:30, once Carson finishes his opening lines.
SAY: You've seen Carson before. This time, watch only how he opens.
ASK: How did Carson grab the sharks at the start?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: what he said first, or showing the board
SCAN for something he said or did, not just the product.
80%+ -> cold call one pair: what did he say next?
Less -> replay the first 30 seconds, re-ask.
ASK: Thumbs: will your pitch grab the sharks that fast?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: mixed, which is fine
trap: remembering the board, not how he opened.
Fix: replay the opening, student names his first move.
notes.prep: Launch. A rewatch with a new job: the hook. Grade 5s saw this clip in Session 1.
notes.sources: Locker Board, Shark Tank US Season 9.

slides.meaning: A short talk that shows your product and convinces people to invest.
slides.example: Our pitch is 60 to 90 seconds, and every team member says a part.

notes.answer: a short talk that shows your product and convinces people to invest
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Pitch. Say it with me. Pitch.
SAY: A pitch is short and shows the product.
It ends by asking for investment. Ours are 60 to 90 seconds.
ASK: Does a pitch ask people to buy, or to invest?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: invest
ASK: How long is our pitch, in seconds?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 60 to 90
trap: ending the pitch with buy it.
Fix: the sharks invest tokens; student rewrites the ask.
notes.prep: One key word, linked to Session 2: sharks invest, they don't buy.

slides.title: The pitch recipe

rows: Who's ever found their hat on the floor?
Hats and bottles fall off bag hooks every day.
Meet Pocket Pal. Hat in, bottle in, hang it up.
Every Pocket Pal is sewn from old jeans.
It costs $2 to make and sells for $8.
Invest your tokens in Pocket Pal!

slides.label: Hook. Problem. Product. Upcycled. Price. Ask.

notes.answer: hook, problem, product and demo, upcycled, price, ask
beats: HOLD UP the Pocket Pal and deliver the whole pitch, about 30 seconds.
Demo it: hat in, bottle in, hang it on a chair.
POINT to each row.
SAY: Six parts, in this order. One sentence each to start.
ASK: Which part did I say first, to grab you?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: the hook
ASK: What did I ask the sharks to do?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: invest their tokens
trap: starting with the product name and skipping the hook and problem.
Fix: say the problem first; the product is the answer to it.
notes.stretch: Which part would you make longer, and why?
notes.help: Cover the right column; say each part's name in order with the student.
notes.prep: The model for SC1 and SC2. Deliver it with energy; you are showing the voice, not just the words.

slides.title: Which part of the pitch?
slides.pivot: read the six parts in order from the board, then re-ask
slides.followUp: cold call one board: how did you know?

items.text: Ever tripped over a tangle of cords?
items.answer: Hook - a question that grabs attention

items.text: Behind every TV is a mess of cords.
Every Cord Keeper is made from old toilet roll tubes.
Invest in Cord Keeper and untangle every lounge room.
Watch: cord in, label on, tidy!

say: Quick round. Write the part of the pitch
trap: calling every first-sounding line a hook.
Fix: ask whether it grabs attention or states a fact, student re-writes.
notes.stretch: Rewrite one line so it's even stronger.
notes.help: Keep the six parts on the board in order.
notes.prep: First decision point: naming parts on a new pitch. Brisk. SC1. Six items, about 5 minutes.

slides.title: Which is the strongest ask?
slides.prompt: The end of the Cord Keeper pitch. Point to A, B or C.

options.misconception: asks the sharks to buy, not invest

options.text: Invest your tokens in Cord Keeper and help us untangle every home.

notes.answer: C - it asks for investment and says what it will do
beats: SAY: The ask is the last thing the sharks hear. Make it count.
ASK: Which is the strongest ask?
15 sec. Cue: voices off. Point... now.
EXPECT: C
SCAN pointing fingers, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call one C: what's wrong with B?
Less -> back to the buying and investing table, re-ask.
REVEAL after fingers are scanned.
SAY: C. It asks for investment and says what it'll do. Tick or fix.
trap: choosing B because it sounds polite.
Fix: ask whether the sharks take a product home, student re-chooses.
notes.prep: Second decision point. Under 80% means every team reads its ask to you before rehearsing.

slides.title: Write it and rehearse it
slides.task: Write your pitch on the planner. Give every member a part. Put your lines on cue cards, then rehearse twice with the timer and your demo.
slides.visualLabel: Write it. Time it. Say it.
slides.extendedTask: a written six-part team pitch on cue cards, rehearsed twice to 60 to 90 seconds with a demo

notes.answer: a six-part pitch, every member speaking, 60 to 90 seconds
beats: SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Everyone, together, on three: Write it. Time it. Say it.
TIME 40 minutes: write 20, rehearse 15, fix 5. At 20, stop everyone.
ASK: Thumbs: does every person in your team have a part?
5 sec. Cue: thumbs at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: thumbs up
CIRCULATE. Listen to one rehearsal per team. Check the ask says invest.
TIME at 5 to go: cue cards and prototype stored together.
trap: one student saying the whole pitch.
Fix: split the six parts across the team, then rehearse again.
notes.stretch: Extension: plan answers to the sharks' questions.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: a sentence starter for every part.
notes.prep: Teams rehearse to a teacher if time allows. Next week is the dress rehearsal with peer feedback.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A team sells pencil cases sewn from old raincoats.
Write a hook and an ask for their pitch.

notes.answer: e.g. Ever had soggy pencils? Invest in Dry Case, keep pencils dry.
beats: SAY: A new product. Work on your own.
ASK: Write a hook and an ask.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a question that grabs attention; invest, not buy
RECORD who writes buy in the ask, or a hook that is just the name.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new product. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Say your part of the pitch to your partner, with your best voice.
slides.selfAssessment: Fist to five: how ready are you to say your part to the sharks?

notes.answer: their own pitch line, said clearly
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: Fist to five: how ready are you to say your part?
5 sec. Cue: fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: mostly three to five
RECORD students showing fists and ones. They rehearse with you first next week.
ASK: Say your part of the pitch to your partner.
30 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first, then swap.
EXPECT: their own line, clear and loud
notes.prep: Next week: dress rehearsal and feedback. Students practise their line at home. SC3.
